warning_rule: chapter count < 60 triggers review; it does not trigger enrichment

chapters.description: Menyatakan suka/tidak suka, kemampuan dasar, pemahaman, dan alasan dengan から.
chapters.reason: After removing unrelated month-name fallback rows, the chapter still has dense hobby/preference nouns, ability verbs, skill adjectives, and reason/question expressions. The actual Reading centers on hobbies, cooking skill, Japanese study, rain-day preferences, and classmates, so no new lexical domain is missing.

chapters.description: Meminta/memberi izin, menyatakan larangan, serta memahami beberapa fungsi ～ています.
reading_evidence: 図書館からのお知らせ
chapters.reason: Permission/prohibition/state grammar is supported by rules, signage, facility-state and safety vocabulary. Reading evidence repeatedly uses library/school/share-house/museum rules; adding unrelated words would not improve the target grammar.

chapters.description: Menggabungkan kegiatan dan sifat dalam satu kalimat dengan bentuk sambung dasar.
chapters.reason: This chapter is deliberately compositional: it connects verbs and adjectives already introduced. Existing routine/connective vocabulary plus cumulative verbs/adjectives is enough for the five Reading contexts; extra chapter-specific words would mostly duplicate prior capability.

chapters.description: Menggunakan bentuk negatif kata kerja untuk larangan, kewajiban, ketidakharusan, dan batas waktu.
chapters.reason: The retained set covers rules, deadlines, health, documents and obligations. Reading evidence focuses on school/company/facility rules and deadlines, so the low count reflects reuse of earlier verbs in ない-form rather than a lexical gap.

chapters.description: Menyatakan pengalaman, daftar kegiatan, dan perubahan keadaan.
reading_evidence: はじめてのアルバイト
chapters.reason: Gate 2C already added independent change/recovery/transitivity verbs. The final set supports experience, lifestyle change, work, town life and travel-preparation readings without reintroducing ～になる constructions as vocabulary.

chapters.description: Mengenal bentuk biasa kata kerja, kata sifat, dan kata benda sebagai dasar menuju pola N4.
grammar_patterns: KB + だ／じゃない／だった／じゃなかった
chapters.reason: Plain-form practice is morphological and intentionally reuses cumulative nouns, verbs and adjectives. The actual Reading is everyday casual narration (yesterday/today/rainy day/weekend), so a larger new lexical inventory is unnecessary.

chapters.description: Menggunakan bentuk biasa untuk pendapat, kutipan, perkiraan, dan kemungkinan.
chapters.reason: The chapter now contains opinion, quotation, prediction, checking, correction, reporting and discussion vocabulary. Reading evidence covers weather forecasts, teacher speech, predictions, reputation and future plans; the remaining low count is not a capability gap.

chapters.description: Menjelaskan waktu, urutan kejadian, dan hubungan otomatis antar kejadian.
chapters.reason: Temporal sequencing, departure/arrival, automatic-event and before/after vocabulary is already broad. The five Reading items directly exercise when/after/until/day-long relations using cumulative action vocabulary.

chapters.description: Menggunakan ～てあげる・～てもらう・～てくれる untuk bantuan dan tindakan demi orang lain.
reading_evidence: 先生に直してもらった作文
chapters.reason: The retained set includes help, entrusting, delivery, care and relationship lexemes needed for ～てあげる／～てもらう／～てくれる. Reading evidence covers homework help, corrected writing, recommendation letters and moving-day assistance.

chapters.description: Membandingkan penggunaan ～たら・～ても・～なら・～ば dalam kalimat kondisi.
chapters.reason: Conditionals are supported by weather, emergency, travel, hazard and state vocabulary. Reading evidence spans rain plans, shopping choices, travel conditions, after-work actions and station arrival; more words would not materially expand conditional practice.

chapters.description: Memberi penjelasan dengan ～んです dan membuat pertanyaan atau permintaan yang lebih natural.
reading_evidence: もう一度お願いします
日本語を勉強する理由
chapters.reason: Explanation/polite-request grammar is supported by service, inquiry, documents, directions and health vocabulary. Reading evidence covers reasons, repeat requests, station directions, study reasons and hospital consultation.

chapters.description: Menggunakan bentuk potensial serta ungkapan batasan seperti ～しか～ない dan ～だけ.
chapters.reason: Potential and limitation grammar chiefly transforms cumulative verbs. The retained set already covers ability, limits, visibility/hearing, skills and practical travel; adding potential forms themselves would violate lexical-role rules.

chapters.description: Menyatakan dua kegiatan bersamaan, beberapa alasan, sebab, dan tujuan.
chapters.reason: Gate 2C added only independent lexemes for commuting, concentrating, moving, balancing activities, going out and calling. Reading evidence directly covers simultaneous activities, reasons and purpose; removed ながら/ので/ために constructions remain excluded.

chapters.description: Menyatakan keadaan hasil, tindakan selesai, keadaan yang disiapkan, dan persiapan sebelumnya.
chapters.reason: After removing the arbitrary 忘れ物確認 collocation, the chapter still has preparation/completion verbs, result-state nouns and common status compounds. Reading evidence repeatedly concerns room/travel/party preparation and completed states, so the lexical capability remains sufficient.

chapters.description: Menyatakan niat, rencana, serta perubahan kemampuan atau keadaan dari waktu ke waktu.
reading_evidence: できるようになったこと
chapters.reason: The count is intentionally low because volitional, ～つもり, ～予定 and ～ようになる are productive grammar, not separate vocabulary rows. The retained lexicon covers goals, plans, education, employment and work conditions; Reading/Listening reuse cumulative actions such as study, practice, work and travel. Further padding would become career-specialist or compositional filler.

chapters.description: Menyatakan usaha membentuk kebiasaan, saran, harapan logis, dan keputusan.
reading_evidence: 先生からのアドバイス
chapters.reason: After removing the arbitrary おすすめ方法 collocation, the chapter still covers habits, advice, decisions, sleep, exercise, health and time management. Reading evidence focuses on daily habits, advice, decisions and transfer plans, all of which can reuse cumulative action verbs.

chapters.description: Menggunakan kondisi dalam situasi nyata dan menyatakan hasil yang bertentangan dengan harapan.
chapters.reason: The retained inventory covers conditions, consequences, viewpoints, pros/cons and contrast discourse. Reading evidence uses real conditions, のに, たとえ～ても, event plans and workplace trouble; extra vocabulary is not required for the grammar contrast itself.

chapters.description: Menjelaskan cara, melakukan percobaan, kemudahan/kesulitan, dan keadaan berlebihan.
reading_evidence: 新しい料理を食べてみる
chapters.reason: The chapter has method/tool nouns, trial/repetition vocabulary and lexicalized ease/usability nouns. The actual grammar derives ～やすい／～にくい／～すぎる and ～てみる from existing lexemes, so derived examples should not be added as separate rows.

chapters.topic: Pola N4 Lanjutan yang Sering Dipakai
chapters.description: Menggunakan pola untuk tahap tindakan, hal yang baru terjadi, perubahan berkelanjutan, dan kalimat pasif.
chapters.reason: The retained community/workplace/practical-Japan inventory is sufficient for passive, ～ところ, ～たばかり and change-over-time patterns. Reading evidence covers current actions, recent arrival, changing town/life and being praised; further additions would drift beyond N4/practical scope.
